# RESULT

## Hypothesis (as-observed, descriptive)

**Original studies report larger effect sizes than their replications in every domain, but the gap is largest in SOCIAL psychology and smallest in EXPERIMENTAL ECONOMICS when "larger" is measured proportionally — whereas measured as an absolute Fisher-z difference the domains are statistically indistinguishable and Cognitive is numerically largest.**

Concretely: originals exceed replications in 73/86 pairs (84.9%), overall mean D_z = fiso−fisr = 0.262 (paired t p=7.1e-12). Because the gap is universal, the domain question is about its magnitude, and the answer is framing-dependent — stated explicitly per domain rather than resolved in favour of one metric.

**(1) Relative/proportional metrics (co-primary #1): Social > Cognitive > Economics in shrinkage.**
mean relative_es 0.278 / 0.509 / 0.657; medians 0.131 / 0.650 / 0.698; |rr|/|ro| 0.411 / 0.639 / 0.724; sign reversals 29.4% / 14.7% / 16.7%; replication success 20.6% / 47.1% / 61.1%. Social ranks 1st (largest gap) in 8 of the 12 tabulated framings, and the Social>Cognitive>Economics ordering is **unchanged in all five robustness variants**. Social−Economics relative_es = −0.378 (bootstrap 95% CI −0.710…−0.054, p=0.022; MW p=0.019) is the one clean separation; Social−Cognitive = −0.231 (CI −0.478…+0.038, boot p=0.089) is clear in medians (0.13 vs 0.65) and ranks (MW p=0.015) but not in means.

**(2) Signed Fisher-z gap D_z (co-primary #2): ordering changes and is not significant.**
Unweighted: Cognitive 0.289 [0.164,0.415] > Economics 0.266 [0.084,0.447] > Social 0.233 [0.162,0.304]. RE(REML): Cognitive 0.234 [0.142,0.326] ≈ Social 0.222 [0.150,0.295] > Economics 0.117 [0.010,0.223]. Between-domain moderator test: **RE Q=2.91, df=2, p=0.234** (vs FE Q=24.9, p<1e-4, which is an artifact of the ee weighting collapse below). RE contrasts: Social−Cognitive −0.017 (p=0.78), Social−Economics +0.099 (p=0.15), rpp−ee +0.105 (p=0.10).

**Mechanism:** Social originals have the smallest baseline effects (mean ro 0.346 vs 0.533 Cognitive), so identical proportional shrinkage yields a smaller absolute z-gap. Exploratory (labelled) meta-regression: se_fiso b=+1.29 (p<1e-6) and fiso b=+0.45 (p<1e-6) dominate; adding original ES renders domain terms null (Social +0.032 p=0.60, Economics −0.079 p=0.28). The gap tracks winner's-curse/significance selection and original imprecision, not a domain-level bias.

**(3) Headline ee weighting diagnostic (n=18).** D_z: unweighted 0.266 [0.084,0.447]; RE(DL) 0.129 [0.011,0.246]; RE(REML) 0.117 [0.010,0.223]; **fixed-effect 0.013 [−0.052,0.078]**. Cause: three studies hold 60.4% of inverse-variance weight (de Clippel AER 2014 alone 43.1%, D_z=−0.155, n=790/780) vs 15.0% top-3 share in rpp. **Stable across weighting:** the proportional-shrinkage ordering (Social worst, Economics best) and the positive sign of every D_z estimate. **Not stable:** whether the ee absolute gap is "small" (RE 0.117) or "absent" (FE 0.013), and which of Social/Cognitive leads on D_z (unweighted/RE → Cognitive; FE → Social). τ² sensitivity is minor (DL 0.025 vs REML 0.017 ee; 0.021/0.022 Social; 0.016/0.016 Cognitive), so this is weight concentration, not a τ² artifact.

**(4) Robustness.** LOO on RE pooled D_z: Social +0.223 (+0.207…+0.241), Cognitive +0.234 (+0.212…+0.250), Economics +0.117 (+0.092…+0.141), rpp +0.227 (+0.217…+0.237), ee +0.117 (+0.092…+0.141) — no single-study driver (max swing 0.049). Contrast jackknife: Social−Cognitive LOO crosses zero (−0.038…+0.009, genuinely null), while Social−Economics (+0.057…+0.129), Cognitive−Economics (+0.071…+0.137) and rpp−ee (+0.062…+0.125) keep positive sign. Variants H2 (Eitam artifact recomputed −0.472→+0.472: Social mean rel_es 0.278→0.306, median 0.131→0.184, ranks unchanged), H3 (po≤0.05 only), H4 (rr>0 only), H5 (rr floored at 0) preserve the relative ordering; in H4/H5 Social ties for largest RE D_z (0.165 vs 0.158). Within every domain originals > replications (paired t / Wilcoxon / 20k sign-flip permutation p≤0.0004; binomial |rr|<|ro| p≤0.004).

**(5) Non-separability.** Economics is exactly the ee project (perfectly nested crosstab) and era is fully confounded with project (34/34 Social and 33/34 Cognitive papers published in 2008, one Cognitive in 2015; all 18 Economics papers 2011-2014; median replication N 58 vs 32 Cognitive / 129.5 Social). Any "domain" difference for Economics is simultaneously a protocol, era and replication-power difference and cannot be decomposed here. `aggregated` and `lab_id` are 100% empty, so multi-effect aggregation and lab clustering are unverifiable; the 86 rows are a significance-filtered selected sample.
